name: Asinelli Tower
desc: 498 wooden steps up a medieval skyscraper that leans just enough to be interesting. Reward: a sea of red roofs.

name: Piazza Maggiore
desc: Bologna's front porch — giant basilica, summer open-air cinema, endless loitering. Sit on the crescentone and just be.

name: Basilica di San Petronio
desc: So big they ran out of money for the facade — half marble, half brick, all charm. Free to gawk.

name: Archiginnasio & Anatomical Theatre
desc: The old university's crest-crusted halls plus a carved wooden theatre where anatomy got theatrical. Pocket-change entry.

name: Portico di San Luca
desc: 666 arches marching uphill to a sanctuary — the world's longest portico and a free cardio pilgrimage with a view.

name: Quadrilatero Market
desc: Medieval lanes stacked with mortadella, fresh pasta and unapologetic cheese. Window-licking costs nothing.

name: Basilica di Santo Stefano
desc: Seven churches nested like Russian dolls on one quiet piazza. A millennium of calm, zero entry fee.

name: Finestrella di Via Piella
desc: A hole in a wall revealing Bologna's secret canal. Thirty seconds of Venice, zero seconds of Venice prices.

name: Giardini Margherita
desc: The city's big green exhale — a lake, turtles, students pretending to study. Picnic-grade happiness.

name: MAMbo
desc: Bologna's modern-art house in an old industrial bakery. Morandi's quiet bottles will rewire your brain for pocket money.
